item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00078","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C13","C05","C24"],"selected_candidate_label":"C13","confidence":0.78,"relationship_type":"both","rationale":"C13 plausibly supplied a concrete drafting template. It is an immediately preceding order in the same Foreign Assistance Act administrative scheme and uses the same core machinery: assigning statutory foreign-assistance functions to a named administrator and making an earlier executive order govern the new administration. The child adapts that structure by transferring functions previously performed by the Secretary of State to the Administrator for Economic Cooperation and preserving the applicability of the referenced orders. C05 is closely related institutionally but chiefly concerns fund allocations and statutory exemptions, while C24 contains similar delegation-and-amendment mechanics in a different program.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"the Administrator for Economic Cooperation shall perform the functions heretofore performed by the Secretary of State","parent_excerpt":"The Secretary of State is hereby authorized and directed to perform the functions of the President","explanation":"Both provisions assign statutorily grounded foreign-assistance functions to a designated executive official; the child adapts the assignment into a transfer from State to the Economic Cooperation Administrator."},{"child_excerpt":"the provisions of that order, as amended by this paragraph, shall be applicable to the operations of the Economic Cooperation Administration under the said Act","parent_excerpt":"The said Title III shall be administered in accordance with the provisions of [DIRECTIVE_REFERENCE] of May 22, 1947","explanation":"Both preserve an earlier executive order as the governing administrative framework for functions newly assigned under 1948 foreign-assistance legislation."}]}
